title: The lamp and the step counter with memory
instruction: Step through the program and answer what it will do. Careful: the same number from the sensor doesn’t always have to give the same result.

steps.input: light = 50, the lamp is on right now
steps.q: What state is the lamp in after this pass through the loop?
steps.why: 50 is neither below 40 nor above 60. No branch applies, so the lamp stays as it was: on.

steps.input: light = 50, the lamp is off right now
steps.q: What state is the lamp in now?
steps.why: The same light as last time, and yet a different result. Between 40 and 60 it’s not the sensor that decides, but memory: the variable lamp. This is called hysteresis.

steps.input: The lamp is off. A car drives past and the sensor shows, one after another, 38, 45, 39, 47, 36.
steps.q: How many times does the lamp switch?
steps.why: At 38 it turns on. The values 45, 39, 47 and 36 don’t turn it off, because none of them is above 60. With the single threshold 40 it would switch 5×.

steps.input: Someone swaps the numbers: if light < 60: on, else if light > 40: off.
steps.q: How does the lamp behave now?
options: it has an even wider calm band
it works like a single threshold of 60 and flickers at the edge again
steps.why: Every number below 60 meets the first condition straight away, and the second branch only applies from 60 upwards. The memory is never used, so only a single threshold is left.

steps.q: How many steps are there at the end?
steps.why: 1600 adds a step and sets up = yes. 1700 and 1600 don’t add anything more. Only 1000 sets up back to no.

steps.q: How many steps are there at the end?
steps.why: 1300 isn’t below 1100, so up stays yes and the second 1600 isn’t counted. A wobbling foot doesn’t count as a new step.

steps.input: You delete the part and up == no from line 5. Measurements: 1000, 1600, 1700, 1600, 1000
steps.q: How many steps are there at the end now?
steps.why: Without memory, every measurement above 1500 adds a step: 1600, 1700 and 1600. So one step is counted three times.

steps.input: You change line 8 to if force < 1500. Measurements: 1000, 1510, 1490, 1520, 1480, 1000 (one step with a wobble)
steps.q: How many steps are there at the end?
steps.why: When both thresholds are the same, the wobble around 1500 flips up back and forth and every new crossing is counted: 1510 and 1520. The band between 1100 and 1500 is what swallows the noise.

debrief: The lamp and the step counter use the same trick: two thresholds and memory between them. Here the variable doesn’t count anything, it just remembers a state. That’s why the device doesn’t flicker and doesn’t count noise. A radiator thermostat works the same way.
